areas.title: vendor-neutral accelerator domain and request contract

proofs.note: Defines normalized vendor, kind, device, request, and selection-policy contracts.
Exposes the vendor-neutral request and response schema at the API boundary.
Covers normalization, compatibility aliases, validation, and invalid combinations.
Documents the compatibility and deprecation boundary for public accelerator fields.

limitations: A vendor-neutral contract does not itself prove that any physical accelerator is available.

areas.title: accelerator persistence and allocation authority

proofs.note: Persists accelerator profiles, allocation authority, and reservation identity.
Enforces concrete allocation ownership and release semantics.
Introduces the durable A2 schema and upgrade contract.
Exercises the PostgreSQL persistence path and authority fields.
Checks migration structure and compatibility invariants.

limitations: Persistence proves database ownership semantics, not device-plugin enforcement on real hardware.

areas.title: pluggable accelerator inventory providers

proofs.note: Implements bounded NVIDIA, Ascend, Kubernetes, fake, and disabled providers plus registry composition.
Validates provider selection, exclusivity, duplicates, and production fake-device restrictions.
Covers fixtures, failure modes, Kubernetes capacity accounting, taints, hardware families, and composition.
Records provider semantics, external Pod accounting, security requirements, and simulated evidence boundaries.

limitations: NVIDIA, Ascend, and Kubernetes discovery fixtures are simulated; real commands and devices remain REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.

areas.title: immutable Runtime Profile contracts

proofs.note: Loads immutable profile identity, version, semantic digest, resources, selectors, and tolerations.
Validates profiles and generated manifest drift.
Pins generated identities and semantic digests for committed profiles.
Defines the machine-readable Runtime Profile schema.
Covers validation, digest stability, generated output, selectors, and security constraints.

limitations: Schema and digest validation do not prove that a profile image runs on declared hardware.

areas.title: logical models and physical vendor variants

proofs.note: Persists logical identity, vendor variants, immutable artifact/profile binding, and audit status.
Enforces ready-variant, last-ready, digest, and status-transition invariants.
Adds the A5 logical-model and physical-variant schema.
Covers repository state transitions and immutable binding rules.
Documents artifact/profile identity and the no-cross-vendor-inference boundary.

limitations: A ready database variant is a control-plane state, not proof of real backend health.

areas.title: accelerator-aware Kubernetes serving renderer

proofs.note: Renders profile-bound resources, selectors, tolerations, security context, and immutable image contracts.
Covers NVIDIA/Ascend resources, security constraints, rendering drift, and invalid profiles.
Defines the serving lifecycle, controller responsibilities, and Kubernetes evidence boundary.

limitations: Renderer and Kind evidence do not establish a production-grade Kubernetes operator or multi-node service.

areas.title: NVIDIA vLLM Kubernetes runtime profile and acceptance contract

proofs.note: Validates NVIDIA runtime diagnostics and acceptance payload semantics.
Pins the NVIDIA vLLM Kubernetes profile and REAL_HW_NOT_RUN status.
Covers validation, diagnostic redaction, and acceptance state transitions.
Records the unexecuted real-hardware acceptance boundary explicitly.
Documents fake-device Kind evidence separately from optional real NVIDIA acceptance.

limitations: Real NVIDIA GPU and vLLM acceptance is REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.

areas.title: Huawei Ascend A2 runtime profile and acceptance contract

proofs.note: Validates Ascend runtime diagnostics and acceptance payload semantics.
Pins the Ascend 910B/A2 profile and REAL_HW_NOT_RUN status.
Covers profile validation, diagnostic parsing/redaction, and acceptance contracts.
Records the unexecuted real Ascend acceptance boundary explicitly.
Separates schema-ready, simulated, and real-hardware evidence states.

limitations: Real Huawei Ascend 910B hardware and vLLM-Ascend acceptance is REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.

areas.title: vendor-aware admission, quota, and fencing

proofs.note: Computes vendor/profile-compatible capacity and fail-closed scale revalidation.
Applies admission decisions, immutable selection snapshots, and quota semantics.
Adds durable selection, admission, and allocation-authority fields.
Covers mixed vendors, homogeneous gangs, fallback policy, quotas, and rejection reasons.
Exercises PostgreSQL admission and serving concurrency semantics.

limitations: Admission uses observed/configured capacity and cannot prove future physical availability or production scale.

areas.title: dual-vendor routing, fallback, circuits, and physical usage

proofs.note: Implements strict/preferred/balanced routing, safe pre-dispatch fallback, SSE pinning, and usage attribution.
Persists vendor circuits and physical serving provenance.
Adds explicit logical-model routing policy and concurrency-safe cursor state.
Exercises PostgreSQL routing cursor and circuit concurrency.
Covers fallback boundaries, SSE behavior, routing policies, circuits, and no-duplicate usage.

limitations: Routing correctness is not a latency SLA and does not establish cross-region or production HA behavior.

areas.title: NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend dual-backend benchmark harness

proofs.note: Runs frozen prompts, warmup/measured phases, buffered/SSE validation, and independent fallback drills.
Covers protocol, semantics, TTFT, aggregation, fallback mode, and failure paths.
Keeps real dual-hardware results explicitly REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.
Documents the operator checkpoint, separate fallback phase, and evidence boundary.

limitations: No real dual-backend throughput, latency, parity, stability, or fallback claim is established.

areas.title: post-A11 serving correctness hardening

proofs.note: Uses dialect-safe bounded candidate snapshots and preserves logical-model/service/quota lock order.
Separates execution ownership from best-effort inventory refresh persistence.
Adds fail-closed service compatibility snapshots and safe upgrade preconditions.
Covers concurrent reconciliation plus autoscaler lock skipping and cursor movement.
Covers migration fail-closed behavior and placement snapshot semantics.
Records upgrade preconditions, quarantine behavior, and operational limits.

limitations: The hardening was validated on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and Kind but not on production HA infrastructure.

areas.title: A11 benchmark correctness review fixes

proofs.note: Starts TTFT at first non-empty content, separates fallback-only execution, and supports exact complete-response matching.
Regresses role-only SSE events, 42 versus 142, Paris versus Parisian, and fallback phase separation.
Prevents corrected harness behavior from being promoted to unrun hardware evidence.
Documents exact/contains matching and the independent operator-driven fallback phase.

limitations: These fixes validate harness correctness only; real NVIDIA and Ascend execution remains REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.

stacked_pull_requests.rationale: The final tree retains the A1 domain and public request contract and extends its tests and compatibility snapshots.
Migration 0011, persistence models, repositories, and allocation-authority tests are present in the final tree.
A3 was reintegrated rather than preserved as a literal ancestor; the final providers, fixtures, configuration, documentation, and expanded inventory tests cover and harden its semantics.
Runtime Profile schemas, semantic digests, manifest generation, validation, and tests remain present and are extended by A7/A8.
Migration 0012 and the logical-model/variant API, persistence, audit, and immutable binding semantics are present.
The accelerator-aware Kubernetes renderer and its profile-bound security/resource tests are present and hardened.
The NVIDIA profile, validators, fake-device Kind contract, acceptance record, and tests remain present with REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.
The Ascend A2 profile, validators, acceptance record, renderer integration, and tests remain present with REAL_HW_NOT_RUN.
